- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.23) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from 10-day moving avg), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–2% for 3–7 day horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.16) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0% to align with momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >+2% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% for next 5–10 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >1.5% in 3+ consecutive days, apply “lag correction” — reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overconfidence in short-term momentum.
- Sentiment volatility >0.30 in 3 consecutive days triggers “sentiment dampening” — reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment swings by 20–30% for next 5 days.
